title: POC scoping: latency & throughput SLO measurement plan - Cyclone Analytics
transcript_header:
Date: 2027-01-14 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Location: Zoom | Recorder: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Jordan Price (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Ethan Morales (Cyclone), Priya Singh (Cyclone), Liam O'Reilly (Cyclone), Nadia Karim (Cyclone)
Meeting purpose: Define TTFT vs TPOT targets, sampling plan, workload sizing and success criteria for a 6-week POC to validate latency/throughput SLOs for chat inference integration.
summary: Align POC acceptance criteria around first-token (TTFT) and total-per-token (TPOT) SLOs; agree sampling methodology (production traces + synthetic replay), target p95/p99 thresholds, test traffic shaping, and timeline for runbook + benchmark deliverables.
topics: TTFT vs TPOT definitions and tradeoffs
sampling size and synthetic replay plan
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Price: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Jordan from Redwood. Quick intro round and we'll jump into the TTFT/TPOT scoping.
[00:10] Ethan Morales: Hi, Ethan here — head of infra at Cyclone. We have about 70k daily active users on chat, look to offload model serving and want guarantees around latency and cost.
[00:25] Maya Chen: Hi Ethan, Maya (Redwood SE). We'll propose a measurement plan that mixes production trace replay with canary sampling. Quick question — are you more worried about perceived latency or token cost?
[00:40] Priya Singh: Perceived latency mostly; product wants sub-600ms median, but legal/customer-facing SLAs ask for p99 targets. There's also budget constraints.
[00:55] Jordan Price: Great. So to be explicit: TTFT is time-to-first-token — what the user feels; TPOT is total per-token time which impacts throughput and cost, right?
[01:10] Liam O'Reilly: Yup. Product cares about TTFT for UX. Engineering will need TPOT to forecast GPU needs.
[01:25] Maya Chen: For the POC we'll propose both: TTFT targets at p95/p99, and TPOT targets measured as per-token latency at p95/p99 for representative payloads. Also include cold-start windows.
[01:40] Nadia Karim: Cold starts are a major concern; our workloads have spikes at 09:00 and 14:00 UTC. We also have long chat threads often hitting 1.2k tokens.
[01:55] Jordan Price: Noted. Let's get into numbers — what thresholds would you consider acceptable?
[02:05] Ethan Morales: From stake holders: p95 TTFT <= 300ms would be ideal, p99 <= 800ms. For TPOT we think p95 per-token <= 12ms and p99 <= 25ms. Those are aspirational but want to validate.
[02:20] Maya Chen: Those are tight but possibly achievable with dedicated fleets and KV cache. Two important clarifications: are those for single-turn chat or multi-turn with KV cache warm?
[02:35] Priya Singh: We need both: cold-path for new sessions and warm-path for active sessions. Acceptance should specify separate buckets.
[02:50] Maya Chen: Good, we'll define buckets: cold (no cache), warm (session KV warmed), and long-sequence (>=1k tokens). We'll also capture median, p95, p99 for TTFT and per-token TPOT.
[03:05] Jordan Price: About sampling — we'd prefer production trace replay instrumented at the API layer plus a synthetic traffic generator to stress tail. How many samples do you have?
[03:20] Ethan Morales: We can provide anonymized request traces for last 30 days — about 1.2M calls; we can sample to create a 10k-50k request replay for the POC.
[03:35] Maya Chen: That works. For p99 stability, we recommend at least 10k samples per bucket, ideally 50k for confidence on high tails. We'll synthesize payloads to cover extremes — long prompts, shorthand prompts, different sampling temperatures.
[03:50] Priya Singh: What's the plan for traffic shaping? We need to see behavior under ramp and steady load.
[03:58] Maya Chen: We'll run a sweep: baseline (low concurrency), ramp (increasing concurrency to expected peak), and stress (1.5–2x peak) for throughput mapping. Each run will be 10–20 minutes per load point to gather stable distributions.
[04:15] Jordan Price: We'll also measure unit economics — tokens per second, GPU utilization, and per-request cost with Redwood's Dedicated vs Hosted comparator.
[04:25] Liam O'Reilly: On instrumentation — we need metrics exported to our Grafana. Can you push metrics and traces?
[04:33] Samir Patel: Yes — Redwood can ship Prometheus-compatible metrics and distributed traces. We'll share a dashboard template and OpenTelemetry fields.
[04:40] Nadia Karim: Security: we need SOC2 alignment, encryption at rest, and customer-managed keys for POC logs. Are logs kept?
[04:48] Jordan Price: For the POC we can configure logging retention and integrate with your KMS. We'll share our security pack after the call.
[04:55] Maya Chen: Back to SLOs — propose the POC acceptance: two separate SLOs per bucket (cold/warm): TTFT p95 <= 400ms, p99 <= 900ms; TPOT p95 <= 18ms, p99 <= 35ms. If Cyclone's targets (300/800 and 12/25) are strict, we can try a dedicated compute profile as an optional line item.
[05:25] Ethan Morales: That seems reasonable as a baseline. We'll aim for initial acceptance at the conservative thresholds and if results are good we'll tune for your tighter targets.
[05:35] Maya Chen: Measurement plan deliverables: 1) traffic sampling definition and replay script; 2) benchmark runbook with load schedule; 3) dashboards and SLO report; 4) cost/perf comparison. We'll run two iterations: canary (10k requests) then full sweep (50k).
[05:55] Priya Singh: Timeline?
[06:00] Jordan Price: Proposed timeline: Week 0 (this week) — exchange traces and credentials; Week 1 — baseline canary run and initial dashboard; Week 2–3 — tuning and full sweep; Week 4 — analysis and runbook handoff; Week 5–6 — optional extended run for compliance and long-term metrics.
[06:20] Liam O'Reilly: Who owns what?
[06:25] Maya Chen: Redwood provides replay scripts, infra templates, and dashboards. Cyclone provides anonymized traces, KMS access for logs, and a small canary token set.
[06:35] Ethan Morales: We'll allocate two engineers to work with you and lock in times for runs during off-peak.
[06:45] Nadia Karim: A note on evaluation: please surface failure modes — partial responses, timeouts, and model fallback latency. We need the runbook to include fallback verification.
[06:58] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll include error categories, SLO burn rate calculations, and automated rollbacks on breach for the pilot.
[07:08] Jordan Price: Pricing/competitors — Ethan asked earlier about Anthropic and in-house options. We'll show Dedicated pricing and the expected unit cost under the POC traffic profile so you can compare against in-house total cost of ownership.
[07:25] Ethan Morales: One more question: warm KV cache eviction policy — how do you model that in benchmarking?
[07:33] Maya Chen: We'll simulate both warm steady-state and cold arrivals by controlling sequence reuse in the replay. We'll also run experiments on different cache sizes to show sensitivity.
[07:45] Priya Singh: For statistical confidence on p99, what's the duration per run?
[07:50] Maya Chen: Recommend at least 10k samples per target to estimate p99 with reasonable CI; that translates to run durations that depend on concurrency. We'll provide guidance in the runbook calculations.
[08:05] Jordan Price: Recap — deliverables and timeline are laid out. Any concerns about privacy or PII in traces?
[08:13] Ethan Morales: We'll scrub PII and use hashed conversation IDs before sending.
[08:18] Jordan Price: Perfect. Let's capture action items.
[08:22] [Meeting shifts to recap and explicit next steps]
[08:25] Liam O'Reilly: Quick clarification: when you say TPOT per-token, are you including tokenization time on our client?
[08:33] Maya Chen: We measure server-side per-token generation; we'll document client tokenization overhead separately to give end-to-end numbers.
[08:40] Nadia Karim: Also include network RTT baseline from our regional PoPs.
[08:46] Samir Patel: We'll add network probes as part of the runbook so we can attribute latencies.
[08:52] Jordan Price: Okay, thanks everyone. We'll send the security pack, replay scripts, and proposed runbook by Friday.
[09:00] Ethan Morales: Thanks all.
[09:03] Jordan Price: End call.
